name: 10MW Floating Offshore Wind Turbine Benchmark
description: Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs) operate in the harsh marine environment with limited accessibility and maintainability. Not only failures are more likely to occur than in land-based turbines, but also corrective maintenance is more expensive. In the present study, a mixed model and signal-based Fault Diagnosis (FD) architecture is developed to detect and isolate critical faults in FOWTs. More specifically, a model-based scheme is developed to detect and isolate the faults associated with the turbine system. It is based on a fault detection and approximation estimator and fault isolation estimators, with time-varying adaptive thresholds to guarantee against false-alarms. In addition, a signal-based scheme is established, within the proposed architecture, for detecting and isolating two representative mooring lines faults. reputation: A specialized engineering benchmark used in floating offshore wind fault diagnosis research, but with limited adoption outside that niche.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on simulated fault detection/isolation in a 10MW FOWT system; results depend on the specific fault classes and simulation setup.
